newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - H.K. newspaper headlines - Sept 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - H.K. newspaper headlines - Sept 16.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- WEN WEI PO - Beijing said Taiwan's efforts to return to United Nations were a political gamble doomed to fail.
-- MING PAO DAILY NEWS - More than 12,000 Hong Kong people took to the streets to join the protest march against the Japanese claim to the disputed Diaoyu or Senkaku islands.

-- Eighty per cent of first year students in China's universities were only children, the highest percentage in history. Some college were planning to set up psychological files to strengthen management over spoiled "little emperors".

-- ORIENTAL DAILY NEWS - Japanese department stores in Hong Kong deployed more security guards on Sunday when demonstrators protesting Japan's claim to the disputed islands urged a boycott of Japanese products.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES - Harbour Centre Development said that it would concentrate on the hotel business in Hong Kong. The group recently bought a site in Western district to build a three-star hotel. The occupancy rate of its hotels was over 90 percent.
-- An American company, GPU Inc, said it was considering buying a stake in Consolidated Electronic Power Asia from Hopewell Holdings.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST - Three senior cadres, propaganda chief Ding Guan'gen, vice-Premier Qian Qichen and Li Lnnqing, had been shortlisted for promotion to China's Politburo Standing Committee in the coming year.

-- HSBC Holdings was poised to become a major player in Formula One racing next season, having clinched a multi-million stg sponsorship deal with Steward Ford Racing Team led by former world champion Jackie Stewart.
